description: A two-panel composite figure of engineering stress–strain curves for two annealed Fe-Mn-Al-C steels; both panels plot Engineering stress (MPa) versus Engineering strain (%). (a) is labelled "Fe-22.5Mn-1.2Al-0.3C [152]"; its y-axis spans 0–1400 MPa (200 MPa ticks) and its x-axis 0–70% (10% ticks), with six curves: CR30%, CR50%, CR30%+630°C/10m, CR50%+550°C/30m, CR30%+700°C/15m and CR50%+700°C/10m. The CR50% dashed-black curve is strongest (rising above the 1200 MPa gridline) but fails below ~5% strain; CR30%+700°C/15m (solid blue) is weakest (peaking near the 700 MPa gridline) yet stretches to ~65%. (b) is labelled "Fe-22Mn-7Al-0.8C [5]" with y-axis 200–1100 MPa and x-axis 0–60%, comparing 800°C/1min, 850°C/1min, 850°C/3min, 900°C/5min, 950°C/5min and 975°C/25min annealing after 50% cold rolling. Increasing annealing temperature/time lowers the peak stress from about 1000 MPa (800°C/1min) to about 760 MPa (975°C/25min) while elongation grows beyond 50%. Together the panels demonstrate the strength–ductility trade-off controlled by cold-rolling reduction and annealing/recrystallization parameters.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots engineering stress (MPa) on a 0–1400 MPa axis against engineering strain (%) on a 0–70% axis.
Panel (a) legend lists exactly six conditions: CR30%, CR50%, CR30%+630°C/10m, CR50%+550°C/30m, CR30%+700°C/15m and CR50%+700°C/10m.
In (a) the CR50% dashed-black curve reaches the highest stress, above the 1200 MPa gridline, but terminates below about 5% strain.
In (a) the CR30%+700°C/15m solid-blue curve is the weakest (peak near the 700 MPa gridline) and the most ductile, extending to about 65% strain.
In (a) the CR30% solid-black curve peaks just above the 900 MPa gridline and fails near 22% strain, whereas CR30%+630°C/10m (solid red) peaks slightly lower and extends to about 34%.
Panel (b) plots engineering stress (MPa) on a 200–1100 MPa axis against engineering strain (%) on a 0–60% axis.
Panel (b) legend lists six annealing conditions: 800°C/1min, 850°C/1min, 850°C/3min, 900°C/5min, 950°C/5min and 975°C/25min.

In (b) the curves are ordered by annealing severity: 800°C/1min is the strongest (peak near the 1000 MPa gridline, failure around 37% strain) and 975°C/25min the weakest (peak near 760 MPa) with elongation beyond 50%.
The sample label printed inside panel (a) reads 'Fe-22.5Mn-1.2Al-0.3C [152]'.
The sample label printed inside panel (b) reads 'Fe-22Mn-7Al-0.8C [5]', i.e. the panel names a single 7Al/0.8C composition whereas the caption describes a Fe-22Mn-(7–10)Al-(0.7–1.0)C series.

The caption states (a) is a Fe–22.5Mn–1.2Al–0.3C steel with different cold rolling and annealing treatments, and (b) a Fe-22Mn-(7–10)Al-(0.7–1.0)C steel with different recrystallization annealing parameters applied after a 50% cold-rolling reduction.
The citing text states that a microstructure with a lower degree of recrystallization provides relatively high strength but lower elongation.

The citing text states that with increasing annealing time and/or temperature the yield behaviour changes from continuous to discontinuous yielding due to the increasing recrystallized volume fraction.
The citing text states that strong increases in yield strength and tensile strength occur due to austenitic grain refinement when a lower annealing temperature and a shorter annealing time are used.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress–strain curves (stress 0–1400 MPa, strain 0–70%) for Fe-22.5Mn-1.2Al-0.3C [152] with six conditions: CR30% (solid black, ~930 MPa peak, ~22% elongation), CR50% (dashed black, >1200 MPa, ~5% elongation), CR30%+630°C/10m (solid red, ~870 MPa, ~34%), CR50%+550°C/30m (dashed red, ~1100 MPa plateau, ~20%), CR30%+700°C/15m (solid blue, ~700 MPa, ~65%) and CR50%+700°C/10m (dashed blue, ~750 MPa, ~62%).

Engineering stress–strain curves (stress 200–1100 MPa, strain 0–60%) for Fe-22Mn-7Al-0.8C [5] after 50% cold rolling and annealing: 800°C/1min (solid black), 850°C/1min (magenta dashed), 850°C/3min (black dashed), 900°C/5min (solid red), 950°C/5min (small-dashed black) and 975°C/25min (solid dark blue). Strength falls and elongation rises with increasing annealing temperature/time.

unreadable_items: Yielding character (continuous vs discontinuous/serrated) cannot be reliably confirmed in the supplied rendering of either panel
